newsitem.title: USA: ARCO Q2 earnings down with products margins.
newsitem.headline: ARCO Q2 earnings down with products margins.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield on Monday said second quarter earnings fell on lower margins for U.S. West Coast refined product sales, but that losses were partly offset by higher oil and gas production.

"Second quarter earnings were reduced by lower West Coast refining margins and lower earnings from ARCO Chemical due to manufacturing plant turnarounds and higher raw materials costs," Mike Bowlin, Atlantic Richfield Co's (ARCO) chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The company earlier reported a net profit of $1.19 per share in the second quarter, versus $1.33 per share a year ago.
ARCO's refining and marketing segment had after-tax earnings of $66 million for the three months ending June 30, down from $129 million a year earlier.
West Coast refining margins were weakened by high operating rates for refiners and large inventories, the company said.
Jet fuel prices fell due to significant imports to the West Coast as well as high refinery production rates.
In 1996, second quarter product prices benefited from short supplies due to a flurry of shutdowns at West Coast refineries.
While earnings were lower than the year earlier period, ARCO's refining and marketing results improved from the 1997 first quarter and the 1996 fourth quarter, the company said.
In addition, sales volumes for refined products showed healthy increases compared to the 1996 second quarter, the company said.
In addition to the integration of more than 200 former Thrifty gas stations into its gasoline station chain, ARCO added 20 new sites during the quarter.

Weaker margins were offset on the upstream, or production said. Overall oil and gas production rose by five percent, led by a 13 percent rise in natural gas production, the company said in a statement.

In the 1997 second quarter, ARCO's worldwide exploration and production operations earned $321 million after tax, compared with $309 million in the same quarter of 1996 despite lower crude and liquids prices.
In chemicals, after-tax earnings from ARCO's 82.5 percent interest in ARCO Chemical Company were $38 million, compared with $75 million in the 1996 second quarter.

Increased volumes and margins in ARCO Chemical's core propylene oxide business were more than offset by higher costs due to plant turnarounds, the expiration of a number of fixed fee MTBE contracts and the impact of higher raw materials prices on other products, the company said.
